newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH SHARES CLOSE HIGHER, HELPED BY BANK GAINS.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH SHARES CLOSE HIGHER, HELPED BY BANK GAINS.

text.p: Swedish shares closed higher on Monday, driven up by a stronger dollar and interest in the banking and insurance sectors.
The Stockholm general index rose 0.56 percent to 3,246.18 after shares worth 4.83 billion crowns changed hands.
Brokers said the half year reports starting to come in looked positive.
"It looks like the business cycle is going well and I think people had underestimated this positive trend," said a broker.
"Overseas investors also seem to be interested in Sweden again," another broker said.

The banking sector peformed well, closing two percent higher. A merger between Switzerland's Winterthur and Credit Suisse triggered renewed interest in the sector and in Sweden speculation about possible mergers started up again, particularly between Handelsbanken and S-E-Banken.
"This has always been one of the rumours and it's a question of how much truth is in it this time," said a broker.

Handelsbanken shares rose 2.50 to 272 crowns while S-E-Banken rose four to 98.50, a day before releasing its half year report. The market was expecting a profit of 3.02 billion crowns against 2.72 billion a year ago.
Nordbanken climbed eight to 284 crowns and insurer Skandia gained eight to 339 crowns.

The market gave its approval to a six month report from medical technology/investment group Incentive and it rose 30 to 730 crowns. Incentive said it was looking at listing its humidity control and water damage unit Munters.
Drugs major Astra closed flat at 142 crowns, losing gains towards the close of trade while the other market heavyweight, Ericsson, closed 2.5 up at 366.5 crowns.
Vehicle maker Volvo gained from the stronger dollar, up 2.5 at 228.-- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
